The Catholic Church. The Roman Catholic Church is the largest Christian denomination in the world, claiming over one billion members and tracing its authority back to Jesus and the Apostle Peter. Centered in Vatican City under the leadership of the Pope, it has shaped European history, culture, and politics across nearly two thousand years, surviving schisms like the Protestant Reformation while maintaining continuity of doctrine and hierarchy.

The Church traces its authority to Jesus's designation of Peter as the rock upon which the Church would be built, recorded in Matthew's Gospel. This became the foundation for papal primacy and the concept of apostolic succession. The Pope serves as the head of the Church and the bishop of Rome. Papal authority developed gradually over centuries, becoming nearly absolute by the Middle Ages, though the Second Vatican Council from 1962 to 1965 introduced more collegial governance.

The Church developed a hierarchical structure running from Pope to Cardinals to Bishops to Priests to laypeople. Its theology of seven sacraments—baptism, confirmation, eucharist, penance, extreme unction, holy orders, and matrimony—distinguishes it from Protestant denominations.

Medieval Catholicism wielded enormous political and economic power, controlling vast lands and taxing populations. The Inquisition, both medieval and Spanish, enforced doctrinal orthodoxy through violence. The Protestant Reformation in the sixteenth century challenged papal authority and Catholic doctrine, leading to the Counter-Reformation of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, which reformed abuses while reasserting Catholic theology and structure.

The Church produced vast theological literature through thinkers like Thomas Aquinas and Augustine, artistic treasures like the Sistine Chapel and Gothic cathedrals, and philosophical traditions. It sponsored science and scholarship alongside periods of obscurantism. Modern Catholicism has grappled with secularization, women's roles, clerical celibacy, birth control, LGBTQ issues, and abuse crises, with Vatican II modernizing the Church's approach to the secular world and other religions.
